reports.conclusion:
Yes, as far as this audit goes: I found no obstruction, and the proof extends to the full CY 4-torus. This is a hand derivation with exact finite-order tests. It is not a written or refereed proof.

The frame-B class stays the same scalar triple w = (E,-e1,-e2). It is not (E,-a1,-(E-a1)), and no colour-dependent class is forced. The singular row stays Gauss hypergeometric, and the leaf poles stay at z = -E/j, because they depend only on the exponent 1 + E/z at Q = 1.

The CY condition enters in exactly one place: it makes w a sum-zero triple, so Theorem L and Theorem VI apply. Off the CY torus, F3 still held in the tests and the leaf structure still has the same derivation. Polar terms appear in the vertex graph already at genus 2 and in edge graphs from genus 3.

A consequence I derived that is new relative to the material: F_g(Q) - F_g(0) = P_g Li_{3-2g}(Q)/(e1 e2) on all of T_CY for g >= 2. That is the Brini-Schuler Rigidity Conjecture for the resolved conifold, which is open in BS_v2 (main.tex line 1531). The argument adds two steps to graph regularity: excluding poles at the discriminant by an a0-adic argument, and regularity at Q = infinity.

Exact tests at generic CY weights passed for all graphs in genus 2 to 5. In genus 4 and 5 this is the first data on the CY torus.
derived: NOTATION. E = a0+a1+a2 = e1+e2, A = a0+a2 = E-a1, B = a0+a1 = E-a2, u = (E-2a1)(E-2a2), tau = 1-1/Q, t = log Q. Non-degeneracy assumed: a1 a2 A B e1 e2 E != 0. Also u = a0^2 - (a1-a2)^2 and 2 a0 E + 4 a1 a2 = u + E^2.

(1) QDE. H*H = (E/tau - a0) H - (a1 a2/tau) 1, so L1+L2 = E/tau - a0 and L1 L2 = a1 a2/tau. Discriminant: delta^2 := tau^2 (L1-L2)^2 = E^2 - (u+E^2) tau + a0^2 tau^2 = (E+a0 tau)^2 - 4AB tau. L_{1,2} = (E - a0 tau +- delta)/(2 tau).
(1) Metric. eta^-1 = e1 e2 [[a0 a1 a2, a1 a2],[a1 a2, -E]].

(1) Picard-Fuchs. z^2 (Q-1) theta^2 - z (a0 + (a1+a2) Q) theta + a1 a2 Q annihilates Int e^{W/z} dU/U = B(-a2/z, A/z+1) 2F1(-a1/z, -a2/z; 1+a0/z; Q). Exponents: Q=0 {0, -a0/z}; Q=1 {0, 1+E/z}; Q=oo {-a1/z, -a2/z}. Only E enters at Q=1.
(1) Singular colour. U_1 -> 1, with root s*(tau) of B tau s^2 - (E + a0 tau) s + A = 0 and s*(0) = A/E. L_1 = A/(tau s*) - a0 = E/t + l_0 + O(t), with l_0 = E/2 - a0/2 - (u+E^2)/(4E).
(1) Regular colour. U_2(0) = -a2/B, L_2 = B s* - a0, L_2(0) = a1 a2/E.

(1) Metric at both colours. Delta_i = e1 e2 (L_i-L_j)(a1 a2 - E L_i) = a1 A e1 e2 W_2(U_i). Delta_1 = -e1 e2 E^3 alg^2/tau^2 = -e1 e2 E^3 t^-2 (1 - u t/E^2 + ...). Delta_2(0) = e1 e2 a1 a2 A B/E. Local coordinate t (or tau), with rho = tau/(t alg), alg^2 = (1-tau s*)^2 phi''(s*)/phi_0''(A/E).

(2) Exact row. With U = 1 - tau s, the Euler phase is phi_tau = A log s + a1 log(1-s) - a2 log(1-tau s), and the thimble is Q^{a1/z} tau^{E/z+1} B(A/z+1, a1/z+1) 2F1(1+a2/z, 1+A/z; 2+E/z; tau). Formal Laplace gives r^pt_{0,1} = Abeta F Ephi alg, with F_n = prod_{j=1}^n (a2+jz)(A+jz) / (n! z^n prod_{j=2}^{n+1}(E+jz)), Ephi = Exp[-dphi/z], dphi' = L_1 - E/tau + A. The same argument as s.3.5-3.7, from the generic amplitude identity and generic (4.4), both hand-checked.

(2) Constants. Abeta = h_{(E,-a1,-A)}(z) E/(E+z): this is Prop 3.15 after rescaling z -> z/A, x = a1/A. By Lemma 13.3 the Q=0 constant is h_nw, nw = (a1, A, -e1, -e2), the same scalar at both colours. So h_nw h_{(E,-a1,-A)} = h_{(E,-e1,-e2)}, because the pairs +-a1 and +-A cancel. The true row at Q=1 is h_{(E,-e1,-e2)} E/(E+z).

(2) Gamma connection, equivalent form. The Stirling tail of Gauss's coefficient Gamma(1+a0/z) Gamma(-1-E/z)/(Gamma(-a1/z) Gamma(-a2/z)) is h_{(-a0,E,-a1,-a2)}, up to the elementary factor from Gamma(-1-E/z). Multiplied by the Gamma-class constant h_{wt_+} it gives h_{(E,-e1,-e2)}. From p_- with a0 -> -a0, a_i -> a0+a_i it gives the same scalar.

(2) Frame B. R' = R_Z h_w^-1 has rows h_{(a1,A,-E)} x Wick, free of e1, e2 except through the overall eta. r_{0,1} = (E/(E+z)) F Ephi alg. rho r_{1,1} = E/t + a1 a2/(E+z) + O(t). The regular colour is non-universal: v_2(z;0) = h_{(a1,a2,A,B,-E,-E)}(z) (1, a1 a2/E). It only needs to be analytic.

(3) Leaves. G = rho r_{0,1} = (E/(E+z)) (tau/t) F Ephi. [t^k](z G) has simple poles only at z = -E/j, j <= k+1, is regular at z=0, and has limit E delta_{k0} at z=oo, since F_n(oo) = 1/(n+1) for all weights. So rho q_t = E + Sum_j A_j lam_j with lam_j = 1/(E - j psi), the same leaves as fibrewise with c -> E, no lam_0 and no polynomial part, and numerator degree <= k.

(3) Closed form of the leaf coefficients. A_j = (-1)^j C_j t^-1 zeta^j 2F1(j B/E, j a1/E; j; tau), zeta = tau e^{dphi/E}, C_j = P_{j-1}/(j! (j-1)! E^{2j-4}), P_k = prod_{i=1}^k ((k+1)a2 - iE)((k+1)A - iE). First correction: q^(1) = (u/2)(lam_1 - lam_2), which explains the factor u in the old point-frame polar data.

(3) Edges and flow. H-row: [t^k] sigma_1 = (E-(k+2)psi) g_{k+1} + Sum l_m g_{k-m} lies in Lam_{k+1}, because t L_1(0) = E. Flow: d/dt[t^2 rho^2 E_11] = Theta Dg(psi) Dg(psi'), Theta = Delta_2/(L_2-L_1) = e1 e2 (a1 a2 - E L_2) = -e1 e2 B tau s* L_2 = O(t). Hence L3 and F3 for E_11. E_11|_{t=0} = -(e1 e2 a1 a2 A B/2) lam_1 lam_1' depends on alpha but dies by Theorem C. L2 for j=2 follows from analyticity of the regular rows.

(3) Comparison with Theorem L. It needs class w, leaf scale = weight E, integer parts, and D(R) <= 2h-3. All hold, with tau_w = -e1/E decoupled from the a's. Theorem L holds in Q(tau) and Cor L3 covers general scale, so no new vanishing is needed. Pole value: (-e1 e2 E^3)^{g-1} Z[g,0] = beta_{2g-2}(e1,e2) by Theorem VI and homogeneity.
(4) Audit, s.1.2. (C1)-(C6) substitution; (C7)-(C8) change: rows now carry h_{(a1,A,-E)}; (C9)-(C12) verbatim.

(4) Audit, s.3. s.3.1-3.3 substitution, with critical polynomial B tau s^2 - (E+a0 tau)s + A. s.3.4-3.5 verbatim, no weights. (3.16) carries over with substitution, using the identity of Remark 3.20. Lemma 3.13 and Thm 3.14 verbatim. Prop 3.15 verbatim after rescaling. Thm 3.17 carries over with the constant line of (2). s.3.10 carries over: P_tr = delta was checked.

(4) Audit, s.4. Lemma 4.1, Lemma 4.2, Prop 4.3 use generic data, already in Prop 13.2(b)(i). Prop 4.4 verbatim. Lemma 4.5 carries over with c/tau -> E/tau - a0, x/tau -> a1 a2/tau, omega = (E+z)/tau - (A+z), checked by hand. Prop 4.6 verbatim. Prop 4.7 carries over: the new eta^{00} entry never touches (0,E). Prop 4.8 verbatim: <(0,E),(0,E)> = -e1 e2 E^3.
(4) Audit, s.5-s.7. s.5 verbatim. s.6 verbatim with l(t) = L_1 - E/t. s.7 verbatim with the Theta above.

(4) Audit, s.8-s.9. Lemma 8.1 verbatim, since the scalar is the same at both colours. Lemma 8.2 substitution. Thm 8.4 is already covered at generic weights by Prop 13.2(b)(ii). Cor 8.5 verbatim. Prop 8.6(a) has a new value. Prop 8.6(b) verbatim. s.9 verbatim. Delta_2'(0) = 0 was observed to persist; it is not used.

(4) Audit, s.13. s.13.0, Lemma 13.0, Theorem C, the string reduction and Theorem R verbatim with c -> E. Lemma A transfer verbatim; this is the only step using the CY condition. Corollary R follows. Verdict: no step fails; most carry over verbatim or by substitution. The one new line is the constant cancellation in (2).

(4) Immediate partial result. On a0 = 0 with free a1, a2, e1, the frame-B rows are literally the fibrewise rows at x = a1/a2, z -> z/a2. So Theorem LC applies by rescaling with no new row analysis. Theorem L is then used at tau = -e1/E, and Prop 13.2 by restriction.

(5) Prop 13.2 is easier on T_CY. Parts (a)-(c), Lemma 13.3 and (F1)-(F9) are already at indeterminate weights. Part (d), the delicate passage to the non-semisimple T_F, becomes a plain restriction with h_nw kept. Part (e) is verbatim.
(5) alpha-independence is not proved in the material. It is BS Conj. rigidity. BS proves only the subtori a_i = e_j (Prop ResConifold, by degeneration) and the case epsilon_+ = 0.

(5) It follows on this route, in three steps. (i) F_g is in Kw(Q), with poles only in {0, 1, oo, Disc = 0}, where Disc = a0^2 + (2 a0 (a1+a2) + 4 a1 a2) Q + (a1-a2)^2 Q^2; its own discriminant is 16 a1 a2 A B, so Disc is irreducible. (ii) No pole at Disc: GW_{g,d} lies in K[[a0]] with K = Q(a1,a2,e1), and one root Q_1 of Disc has a0-adic valuation 2. Substituting Q = Q_1 into N = F_g Disc^m D' forces N(Q_1) = 0, hence Disc | N. (iii) No pole at oo for a1 != a2: L_i -> {a1, a2} and W_2 stays finite and non-zero at both colours. With the polar part gap_g t^{2-2g} at Q=1, the difference F_g - F_g(0) - P_g Li_{3-2g}/(e1 e2) is a polynomial bounded at oo that vanishes at Q=0, so it is 0.

(5) Conversely, if rigidity were known separately, the total gap on T_CY would reduce to the T_F result, but graph-by-graph regularity would not follow. A separate total-level route without graphs: F_g^inst = Sum_{l<=2g-2} c_{g,l} Li_{1-l}, and e1 e2 x (F_{g,d} - value) vanishes on a_i = e_j and on E = 0, and is invariant under (a1,a2) -> (E-a2, E-a1). With lambda_g^2 = 0 this gives rigidity for g = 2 only; at g = 3 it leaves one unknown number per d. It does not reach all genera.

obstructions: None found. No audited step fails on T_CY.
Mild scope conditions. Graph regularity needs a1 a2 A B e1 e2 E != 0. Q = oo needs a1 != a2. The total formula extends to the excluded loci by polynomiality of e1 e2 GW_{g,d} on T_CY.
Off the CY torus Theorem L and Theorem VI are unavailable (class (Ea,-e1,-e2) is not a sum-zero triple), and the tests show real polar terms there. So the extension stops exactly at T_CY.
The total-level shortcut through BS Prop ResConifold plus polynomial divisibility does not reach all genera; it stops after g = 2.

Step 1. Rewrite s.1.2-s.9 with the dictionary (phi_tau, s*, delta, L_i, Delta_i, alg, omega, Theta, F_n, P_k, eta^-1) and prove Theorem LC_CY. Only the substituted identities need re-derivation; s.3.4-3.5, s.5-s.7 and s.9 follow the existing text.
Step 2. Prop 13.2_CY: take (a)-(c), (e) at indeterminate weights, restrict to the hyperplane, and record h_nw h_{(E,-a1,-A)} = h_w.
Step 3. Corollary R_CY: Theorem R with c -> E, Cor L3 at w = (E,-e1,-e2), Theorem VI by homogeneity.
Step 4. Corollary (rigidity): the Disc lemma plus regularity at Q = oo plus Step 3 give the closed form for g >= 2, recovering BS Prop 3.1 on T_F without degeneration. Treat g = 0, 1 separately.

Step 5. Referee the rewritten text, especially the constant cancellation, the a0-adic lemma, and the claim that poles lie only in {0, 1, oo, Disc}. Optionally add a direct evaluation at Q away from 1 for g = 4, 5.

reports.conclusion:
Finite-order tests say yes, and no obstruction appeared. On the full CY 4-torus the same frame works: w = (E,-e1,-e2) with the scalar Hodge class Omega_w, R' = R_Z h_w^-1. At genus 2, 3 and 4, at generic weights including random F_p residues, every coloured stable graph with an edge is regular at Q = 1. The single-vertex graph has polar part exactly P_g (2g-3)!/(e1 e2) t^(2-2g). Every decorated graph obeys pole order <= Sum_v (2g_v-2)_+, with the same tallies as on the fibrewise torus. This is evidence, not a proof.

The mechanism I derived by hand is that the deformation only touches the leaves. The singular row stays hypergeometric with 2F1(a2/z+1,(a0+a2)/z+1;E/z+2;tau), so the leaf poles stay at z = -E/j. The vertex class and leaf scale, and hence M_irr and the pole value, depend only on (e1,e2). So Theorem R and Theorem L should carry over unchanged, and the work left is a three-parameter rewrite of Theorem LC plus restricting the already generic Prop 13.2(a)-(c) to the CY hyperplane. No step of this has been written or refereed. Frames (i), (iii) and the actual fixed-point classes fail: all edge graphs are singular there. Only the colour-1 class matters; the colour-2 class is free in every choice tested. Off the CY locus, regularity fails at genus 3 in exactly the graphs with a vertex of genus >= 2, which points to Theorem L as the only place CY enters.
derived: All formulas below were derived by hand and also checked in exact arithmetic (see tested). Notation: A = a1, B = a0+a2 = E-a1, C = a2, tau = 1-1/Q, u = (E-2a1)(E-2a2).
Frobenius data: eta^-1 = e1 e2 {{a0 a1 a2, a1 a2},{a1 a2, -E}}. L_1+L_2 = E/tau - a0 and L_1 L_2 = a1 a2/tau. QDE matrix A_QDE = [[0,1],[-a1 a2/tau, E/tau - a0]].

Delta_1 t^2 -> -E^3 e1 e2, independent of alpha (from L_2(0) = a1 a2/E). More precisely Delta_1 = -E^3 e1 e2 alg^2/tau^2, where alg^2 = (AB/E^3) U_1 [A(1-tau)/(1-s*)^2 + B/s*^2] and alg(0) = 1. Also Delta_2(0) = e1 e2 a1 a2 (a0+a1)(a0+a2)/E.

Euler coordinate U = 1 - tau s, phase phi_tau(s) = B log s + A log(1-s) - C log(1-tau s). Critical equation: (a0+a1) tau s^2 - (E + a0 tau) s + B = 0, with s*(0) = B/E. Discriminant: delta^2 = E^2(1-tau) - u tau + a0^2 tau^2.

Frozen row: r^pt_{0,1}(z;0) = h_{(E,-a1,-(a0+a2))} E/(E+z). This is Prop 3.15 rescaled, using only Stirling for B(A/z+1,B/z+1). With the QRR constant h_nw, nw = (a1,a0+a2,-e1,-e2), the a1 and a0+a2 factors cancel exactly, so r_{0,1}(z;0) = h_{(E,-e1,-e2)} E/(E+z). This forces the frame w = (E,-e1,-e2) at colour 1 for every alpha.

Decoupling: r' = h_{(a1,a0+a2,-E)} r^pt, so frame-B rows do not depend on (e1,e2) at fixed (a0,a1,a2). Delta_i and E_ij are proportional to e1 e2. So each frame-B term is (e1 e2)^(g-1) times Hodge integrals of Omega_w (dependent on e only) times factors dependent on a only.

KEY FORMULA, generic form: rho r'_{0,1} = (E/(E+z))(tau/t) 2F1(C/z+1,B/z+1;E/z+2;tau) Exp[-dphi/z], with F_n = prod_{j=1}^n (C+jz)(B+jz)/(n! z^n prod_{j=2}^{n+1}(E+jz)). Since F_n(oo) = 1/(n+1) as before, the arguments of Lemmas 5.1-5.2 and the sum rule are formally the same.

First leaf: [t^1](z rho r_{0,1}) = (u/2)(lam_1 - lam_2), with rho^-1 = 1 - u t/(2E^2) + ... Top leaf: a_{k+1}^(k) = (-1)^(k+1) P_k/((k+1) k!^2 E^(2k-2)), P_k = prod_{j=1}^k ((k+1)a2 - jE)((k+1)(a0+a2) - jE). The fibrewise sharpness loci move, but the upper bound is unaffected.
Flow: Theta = e1 e2 (a1 a2 - E L_2) = Delta_2/(L_2 - L_1), with Theta(0) = 0.

Symmetry: swapping the fixed points, (a0,a1,a2) -> (-a0,a0+a1,a0+a2), exchanges B and C and preserves u. This explains why polar coefficients are polynomials in (u, a0^2). (Their degrees and divisibility are tested, not derived.)

M_irr, (H0) and Theorem VI are statements about (w, leaf scale E) only, since homogeneity reduces them to x = e1/e2. So the fibrewise statements apply unchanged if the leaf bounds hold. This is taken from the statement of Theorem R and s.13; LEMMA_A_PROOF.md was not opened.

Exactly one is singular, the vertex graph at colour 1, so colourings need not be summed. Coloured decorated orbits of graphs with all g_v <= 1 are individually regular. Where a vertex has genus >= 2, individual decorations are singular and only the decoration sum at fixed colouring is regular. In the point frame every decorated graph is singular with pole 2g-2 and the poles cancel only in the total.

Other frames, S1 and S3, g = 2, 3: actual fixed-point classes (wt+, wt-) and the swapped assignment are singular on all edge graphs (6/6, 41/41). So is nw at both colours. c1=B with c2=wt+ or wt- is regular (0/6, 0/41).

Rows twisted by h_w with vertex class (E+1,-e1,-e2): total wrong. s = +1: total wrong. Wrong but consistent classes (-E,e1,e2) and (E+1,-e1,-e2): total correct, as a frame change must give, but all edge graphs singular. The correct frame passes in the same runs.

Leaf tests directly from the Wick rows at fibrewise, S1, S2, S3 and random residues: KEY FORMULA (t^0..t^7, z^0..z^12). L1 for k <= 7 (overdetermined by 14 equations): leaves in Lam_{k+1}, sharp except where P_k = 0, as the formula predicts (for example k = 3 at S1). L3 for k <= 5 (78 equations), anti-diagonal needed. L2 for j = 1, 2, b <= 3, k <= 5. E_21(b,a) = E_12(a,b). F2 with [t^0] rho r_{1,1} = a1 a2/(E+z). F3: all Dil and E have valuation >= 0. Second QDE row at both colours to z^11. Symplecticity to w^12. The E_11 flow with Theta above, m+n <= 11.

Alpha dependence, frame B, fixed (e1,e2) = (5,11), 20 alpha samples, decorated graph by decorated graph. Coefficient of t^(2-2g): independent of alpha. t^(3-2g): u times a constant. At g = 3: t^-2 is polynomial of degree 2 in (u, a0^2), t^-1 of degree 3 and divisible by u. Example, (5,11) sample vs S1, g = 2, dec with no dilaton: t^-2 -2/45 in both; t^-1 -1/160 vs 1/72, ratio equal to u ratio -36/80.

Off the CY locus, frame (Ea,-e1,-e2), Ea = a0+a1+a2 != e1+e2, at (a0,a1,a2,e1,e2) = (2,3,4,5,11), (3,3,4,5,11), (1,7,2,5,3): the row still freezes, r'_{0,1}(z;0) = Ea/(Ea+z), and Delta_1 t^2 -> -Ea^3 e1 e2. At g = 2 edge graphs are regular but the vertex graph gains t^-1. At g = 3 stable graphs 1, 2, 5, 6 are singular. (The t^-3 term at the first of these runs is what shows the vanishing is lost.)
Limits: g <= 4; g = 4 frame B only; z-order <= 12 in the leaf tests; F_p zero tests are probabilistic; finite weight samples. Everything is evidence, not proof.
obstructions: No obstruction to the extension was found in any test.

The frame is rigid at colour 1: (E,-a1,a1-E), (E,-a2,a2-E), the actual fixed-point classes, nw, (-E,e1,e2) and (E+1,-e1,-e2) all give singular edge graphs at generic alpha. So the fibrewise coincidence a_i = e_i cannot be exploited by any class built from the a's.

CY cannot be dropped: off CY the leaves still freeze, but vertex graphs and graphs with a vertex of genus >= 2 stay singular. This suggests Xi_h != 0 for a non-CY class. The genus-3 graph data shows it; I did not compute Xi_h directly.

This route gives only the polar part. It does not prove the closed form F_g - F_g(0) = P_g Li_{3-2g}(Q)/(e1 e2) on the CY torus; that closed form is tested only (g <= 4, to t^2 at g = 4), and [BS] Prop 3.1 covers T_F only.
Excluded weights: a1, a2, a0+a1, a0+a2, e1, e2 and E must be non-zero, since the Frobenius data or the class degenerates there.
pathway: Step 1 (Theorem LC_CY): rewrite s.3-s.11 of leaf_structure_proof.md with (x,1,1) -> (A,B,C), c -> E. Abeta at t = 0 needs only rescaling of Prop 3.15. The eikonal/transport proof carries over with Eik(p) = tau(1-tau)p^2 + (E-(B+C)tau)p - BC and P_tr = delta. Then L1 (Lemmas 5.1-5.2), s.6 with sigma^(-1) = (0,E) and sigma^(0) = (E lam_1, a1 a2 lam_1), the flow with Theta above, and s.9 (which uses only analyticity of v_2 at t = 0).

Step 2: Theorem Q at generic weights is already in Prop 13.2(b)(ii),(iv) (row 2 via PF and km, symplecticity from Q = 0). So the conjugate-encoding part of s.8 and the K_1 = 1 step should not need redoing. Analyticity of v_2 at t = 0 follows from U_2(0) = -a2/(a0+a1) and Delta_2(0) != 0.
Step 3: Theorem R and Corollary R unchanged, with c -> E and -x c^3 -> -E^3 e1 e2. M_irr (Theorem L), (H0), Theorem C and Theorem VI are applied to w = (E,-e1,-e2) as they stand.

Step 4 (Prop 13.2_CY): parts (a)-(c) and Lemma 13.3 are already written at indeterminate five weights. Either restrict to the CY hyperplane, where all denominators are products of a1, a2, a0+a1, a0+a2, e1, e2 and a0 (and the non-constant ratio in (F8) persists), or repeat them over Q(a1,a2,e1,e2). Then part (e) with w = (E,-e1,-e2). Part (d), the passage to T_F, is not needed at a0 != 0. The loci a0 = 0 follow by rationality in the weights. The rows are elements of the quadratic algebra over Kw(Q), so no connection problem arises between Q = 0 and Q = 1.

A low-cost first move, if wanted: have one agent do Step 1 and a referee re-derive the generic s.3 and s.7, since those are where B = C could be hidden in an identity.

Genus >= 5 at generic weights: not tested. Colour-2 class freedom: tested only for the classes listed, at g <= 3.
No proof that polar coefficients per decorated graph are polynomials in (u, a0^2) with the observed degrees, nor that odd orders are divisible by u (flop symmetry suspected, not checked).
Whether the closed form for F_g holds on the CY torus in all genera.

crit.conclusion:
Most honest answer: yes in substance, but it is not yet a theorem of record. I found no obstruction and could not refute either report.

The extension to the full CY 4-torus reduces to one piece of unwritten work: a generic-parameter rewrite of Theorem LC (call it LC_CY). I expect this to need no new idea, because every other ingredient already covers T_CY:
- Theorem L and Cor L3 hold at w = (E,-e1,-e2), with leaf scale E.
- Theorem VI depends only on (e1,e2).
- Prop 13.2 (a)-(c), (e) is already stated at indeterminate weights.
- Theorem R uses only support bounds. Each Xi_h(R) vanishes separately, so the alpha-dependent leaf coefficients never need to satisfy any relation. This is why the alpha-dependence is harmless.

The CY condition enters for one reason. The row scale is a0+a1+a2, and the class must be a sum-zero triple whose first weight equals that scale, which forces a0+a1+a2 = e1+e2.

Two things are stronger than a pathway:
1. The three-torus a0 = 0 with a1, a2, e1 free follows at once from the existing Theorem LC by rescaling. This is my reading of the argument; no short note has been written.
2. Report 1's extra claim survives my attack: Cor R_CY implies F_g - F_g(0) = P_g Li_{3-2g}(Q)/(e1 e2) on all of T_CY, which is the BS Rigidity Conjecture for the conifold. I checked its three hand steps. Report 2's statement that the route gives only the polar part is superseded by this argument.

New evidence from this audit, independent of the R-matrix: direct virtual localisation at fresh T_CY weights matches the closed form for all (g,d) tested, up to g = 7 at d = 1. Exact rational reconstruction in Q at g = 2, 3 shows the claimed pole structure.

Caveat: the rigidity corollary is new and nothing here has been refereed. My two genus-5 runs had not finished when this report was forced, so they give no result. Genus 5 evidence is still Report 1's single sample.
derived: All items here were re-derived by hand by me. Notation: E = a0+a1+a2 = e1+e2, A = a0+a2, B = a0+a1, u = (E-2a1)(E-2a2), tau = 1-1/Q.

FIRMLY ESTABLISHED, Frobenius data. From PF: tau L^2 - (E - a0 tau) L + a1 a2 = 0. Metric: eta = (1/(A B e1 e2)) [[E/(a1 a2),1],[1,-a0]], inverse e1 e2 [[a0 a1 a2, a1 a2],[a1 a2,-E]], confirmed from wt_+, wt_-. (a1 a2 - E L_1)(a1 a2 - E L_2) = a1 a2 A B, so Delta_i = e1 e2 (L_i-L_j)(a1 a2 - E L_i).

FIRMLY ESTABLISHED, discriminant. Q^2 tau^2 (L1-L2)^2 = Disc = a0^2 + (2 a0(a1+a2)+4 a1 a2) Q + (a1-a2)^2 Q^2, and disc(Disc) = 16 a1 a2 A B. Critical polynomial: B Q U^2 - (a0 + Q(a1-a2)) U - a2 = 0, whose discriminant is Disc.

FIRMLY ESTABLISHED, Lemma 13.3 at both roots. Beta tails: Wick_+(Q=0) = Exp[b(-a2 + A - a0)] and Wick_-(Q=0) = Exp[b(a0 + a1 - B)], writing v for v^(1-2k), with b the coefficient b_k z^(2k-1). So h_nw Wick_+- = h_{wt_+-}. The same scalar h_nw works at both colours, for any weights.

FIRMLY ESTABLISHED, frozen row. B(A/z+1, a1/z+1) divided by its stationary-phase normalisation equals (E/(E+z)) Exp[b(A + a1 - E)] = h_{(E,-a1,-A)} E/(E+z). Then h_nw h_{(E,-a1,-A)} = h_{(E,-e1,-e2)}, so frame B with w = (E,-e1,-e2) gives r_{0,1}(z;0) = E/(E+z). No analytic connection problem arises, because each z-coefficient of a row is algebraic on the curve.
FIRMLY ESTABLISHED, colour 2 at Q = 1. r^pt_{0,2}(z;0) = h_{(a2,-E,B)} and v_2(z;0) = h_{(a1,a2,A,B,-E,-E)}(z) (1, a1 a2/E). The second factor follows from the tau^-1 part of QDE row 2.

DERIVED, key formula. The Euler integrand is s^(A/z)(1-s)^(a1/z)(1-tau s)^(-a2/z-1), so the row is 2F1(1+a2/z, 1+A/z; 2+E/z; tau) and F_n = prod_{j=1}^n (a2+jz)(A+jz)/(n! z^n prod_{j=2}^{n+1}(E+jz)), with F_n(oo) = 1/(n+1). The eikonal equation tau(1-tau)p^2 + (E-(a2+A)tau)p - a2 A = 0 has discriminant equal to delta^2, and its regular branch has p(0) = a2 A/E.

DERIVED, first orders. Delta_1 = -e1 e2 E^3 t^-2 (1 - u t/E^2 + ...). [t^1] G = u/(2(E+z)(E+2z)), so [t^1](zG) = (u/2)(lam_1 - lam_2). Sign trap, not an error: on T_F u = -(1-x)^2, so this agrees with F1 and with (a_1,a_2) = ((1-x)^2/2)(-1,1) of the proof.

DERIVED, H-row. rho r_{1,1} = L_1 G + z (tG)'/t. Its t^-1 term is (E+z) g_0 = E. Its t^0 term is (u/2 + l_0 E)/(E+z) = a1 a2/(E+z), with l_0 = E/2 - a0 - a1 a2/E. [t^k] has factor (E+(k+2)z) on g_{k+1} because t L_1(0) = E, the same E as the leaf scale. This matching is the structural reason L2 and L3 survive.

DERIVED, flow. L_2 = B s* - a0 and a1 a2 - E L_2 = B(A - E s*) = -B tau s* L_2. So Theta = -e1 e2 B tau s* L_2 = O(t), and E_11|_{t=0} = -(e1 e2 a1 a2 A B/2) lam_1 lam_1'. Only Theta(0) = 0 is used for F3 and L3.

DERIVED, a0 = 0 three-torus. There h_nw h_w^-1 = h_{(a1,a2,-E)}, so frame-B rows depend only on (a1,a2) and are the T_F rows at x = a1/a2, z -> z/a2. e1, e2 enter only through eta^-1 (the factor e1 e2) and through Omega_w. So Theorem LC plus Theorem R with tau_w = -e1/E applies directly.

DERIVED, rigidity step (i). Rows have poles only at Q in {0,1,oo} or at Disc = 0. U = 1 forces A(Q-1) = 0; QU = 1 forces a1(1-Q) = 0; a1 a2 - E L_i = 0 only at tau = 0. Colour-summed graphs lie in Kw(Q). Q = 0 is regular since a0 != 0.

DERIVED, rigidity step (ii), Disc lemma. GW_{g,d} lies in K[[a0]] with K = Q(a1,a2,e1), as in Prop 13.2(d). Write F_g = N/(Disc^m (1-Q)^n) with m minimal. N = F_g Disc^m (1-Q)^n has coefficients in K[[a0]]. The root Q_1 of Disc has valuation 2 and lies in K[[a0]] by Hensel, so evaluation at Q_1 is a ring map and N(Q_1) = 0. Disc is irreducible over K(a0), since a1 a2 A B is not a square, so Disc | N and hence m = 0.

DERIVED, rigidity step (iii), Q = oo. For a1 != a2, L -> {a1,a2}; U -> (a1-a2)/B or QU -> -a2/(a1-a2); Delta_i is finite and non-zero, equal to -a1 B (a1-a2) e1 e2 and its partner. Rows are analytic in 1/Q. With Li_{3-2g}(e^t) = (2g-3)! t^(2-2g) + regular and Li -> 0 at Q = 0 and oo, the difference is a constant that vanishes at Q = 0. The result extends across a1 = a2 and E = 0 as an identity of rational functions on T_CY.

DERIVED consequence: F_g(oo) = F_g(0), i.e. constant-map terms of X and of its flop agree on T_CY, with flop weights (a1-a2, a2, A, -e1, -e2) and (a2-a1, a1, B, -e1, -e2). I derived the flop weights from the conifold generators of weights a1, A, a2, B.
CONDITIONAL. Theorem R, Lemma 13.0 and (H0) go through verbatim with c -> E, -x c^3 -> -e1 e2 E^3. So LC_CY implies Cor R_CY, and with the rigidity steps above it implies the closed form.

NOT DERIVED by me: the line-by-line generalisation of s.3-s.9 (including the sum rule of s.5 and the z = 0 regularity argument of s.3.10). I read only s.0, s.9, s.13 and s.14 of the proof, and the statements of LEMMA_A_PROOF.md, and I spot-checked the reports' identities rather than rewriting the text.
tested: All runs are exact in F_p, p = 2^127-1, at weights not used by either report unless noted. Each is finite-order evidence, not proof. Logs are in cy_torus_explore/critic/.

NEW, independent of the R-matrix: direct virtual localisation of GW_{g,d} (my own graph enumeration and edge/vertex formulas; Hodge integrals from row_audit/hodge_engine.py) equals P_g d^(2g-3)/(e1 e2). Passed: g <= 6, d = 1 at (7/5,-3/8,13/6,11/9); g <= 5, d <= 3 at (-5/4,19/7,2/3,17/5); g <= 4, d <= 4 at (3/2,-1/3,5/7,8/3); g <= 7, d = 1 at (3/4,-2/5,9/7,13/3); g <= 4, d <= 2 at E = 0 sample (1,2,-3,5,-5) and at a1 = a2 sample (2/3,5/4,5/4,1/7). Genus 0 and genus 1 also matched (expected 1/(d^3 e1 e2) and P_1/(d e1 e2)). Non-CY control (7/5,-3/8,13/6,11/9,2): fails for all g >= 1.

NEW: frame-B graph sum at a random Q0 in F_p, Q = Q0 e^t, away from Q = 1. Total equals P_g Li_{3-2g}(Q)/(e1 e2) + F_g(0) on t^0..t^4 at g = 2, 3, 4 at (7/5,-3/8,13/6,11/9) and at g = 3 at (-5/4,19/7,2/3,17/5). The class (E,-a1,-A) at g = 2 and the point frame at g = 3 give the same total, as a frame change must. Non-CY control with class (Ea,-e1,-e2): fails at g = 2, 3.

NEW: exact rational reconstruction in Q from 60-70 evaluations, frame B. g = 2: total (1-Q)^-2 with deg N = 2; each of the 6 edge graphs Disc^-4 with deg N = 8; vertex graph Disc^-4 (1-Q)^-2 with deg N = 10. g = 3: total (1-Q)^-4 with deg N = 4; all 41 edge graphs Disc^-8 with deg N = 16; vertex graph Disc^-8 (1-Q)^-4 with deg N = 20. So individual graphs have Disc poles that cancel in the total, edge graphs are regular at Q = 1, and all are regular at Q = oo. Point frame at g = 2: all graphs have (1-Q)^-2.

NEW: constant-map flop identity F_g(0) = F_g^flop(0) passed for g = 2..6 at two CY samples and failed for g = 2..6 at non-CY (1,2,4,3,5). F_g(0) itself does depend on alpha (g = 2, 3, 4, three alpha samples at fixed e1, e2), so rigidity concerns only the part with Q-dependence.

RE-RUN, row_audit code, frame B, g = 2, 3, 4. Every sample gave edge colourings 20/20, 350/350, 8596/8596 regular, vertex graph with only t^(2-2g), and total matching for t^(1-2g)..t^3 except t^0. Fresh generic samples: (7/5,-3/8,13/6,11/9), (-5/4,19/7,2/3,17/5). Special samples: u = 0 (1,3,2,5/2); e1 = e2 (3/2,-1/3,5/7,79/84); a1 = a2 (2/3,5/4,5/4,1/7); a1 = a2 with e1 = e2 (2,3/5,3/5,8/5); 3 a2 = E (1,3,2,7/5); a0+a2 = a1 (1,3,2,1/9); T_F itself (0,5/3,2/7,5/3); negative-weight sample with small E (-3,1,5/2,7); a1 = -a2 (5,7/3,-7/3,2); a0 = a1 (4/3,4/3,1/5,3). No special sample broke regularity, so it is not an artefact of a generic sample.

RE-RUN, exact_test code, at (7/5,-3/8,13/6,11/9): singular stable graphs = vertex graph only, of 7, 42, 379 at g = 2, 3, 4, total ok. The two reports' codes are independent of each other and agree with mine on the samples compared.

NEW: L1 from Wick rows at (2/9,11/4,-7/6,3/5): [t^k](rho q_t) prod(E-j psi) has degree exactly k for k = 1..10 (k = 0 gives degree 1, the constant E), tested through psi^19. E_11 bi-degree bound for k <= 6, m+n <= 14: 0 violations out of 71-119 tests per k. rho_1 = u/(2E^2) confirmed. This extends the reports' k <= 7.

Limits: finite genus, degree, t and z orders; F_p zero tests are probabilistic. Frame dependence is inherent: regularity graph by graph holds in frame B and fails in point and (E,-a1,-A) frames (reports' tables and my reconstruction at g = 2 point frame), while totals are frame-independent. Two genus-5 runs of mine (generic Q0 at (2/9,11/4,-7/6,3/5), and Q = 1 at (-5/4,19/7,2/3,17/5)) were still running with empty logs when this report was forced, so they give no result.
obstructions: None found. I tried: special weight loci, a fresh independent localisation test, generic Q, a Hodge-level flop consequence, and a search for steps using a2 = A or a_i = e_i. None produced a failure.

Off T_CY the extension genuinely stops. The total has all polar orders, and localisation at (g,d) fails for every g >= 1 tested. The leaf structure itself survives off CY according to both reports' tests; what is lost is the sum-zero class needed for Theorem L and Theorem VI.

Scope conditions for the graph statement: a1 a2 A B e1 e2 E != 0. E = 0 is outside frame B, though the closed form extends there as a rational-function identity (localisation at the E = 0 sample agrees). The Q = oo step needs a1 != a2, removable the same way.

Corrections to the reports. Report 2's limit 'polar part only' is superseded by Report 1's rigidity steps, which I checked by hand. Report 1's wording 'the proof extends' should read 'extends subject to writing and refereeing LC_CY'. Report 1's False at a0 = 0 for the constant term is an artefact: F_p code computes inv(0) = 0 there, as Report 1 says. Report 1's total-level shortcut to rigidity at g = 2 was not checked by me.
pathway: Step 1 (short, can be done now): state the a0 = 0 three-torus theorem as a corollary of Theorem LC, Theorem R, Cor L3 at tau = -e1/E and Theorem VI by homogeneity. Prop 13.2 by restriction, keeping h_nw.

Step 2 (the only real work): write LC_CY by replacing (x,1,1), c with (a1,a2,A), E throughout s.3, s.5, s.6, s.7, s.9. Row 2 of the QDE and symplecticity (s.4.6, s.4.8, s.8.4, s.8.5) can be taken from Prop 13.2(b)(ii),(iv) at generic weights, extended to a0 = 0 by rationality, rather than re-proved.

What is hard in Step 2, roughly in order. First, s.3.5-s.3.7 and s.3.10 (identifying the Wick row with the Euler expansion and proving z = 0 regularity) carry the most identities in which a2 = A could be hidden. Second, the s.5 sum rule and the absence of a polynomial part. Third, s.7 flow bookkeeping. I expect no new idea: the eikonal, F_n, Theta and first-order values already check by hand. My estimate is about one writing round plus two independent referees, comparable to earlier rounds. This is a judgement, not a measured figure.
Step 3: Cor R_CY from Theorem R with c -> E, plus the one-line constant cancellation h_nw h_{(E,-a1,-A)} = h_w.

Step 4: Corollary (rigidity for the conifold): Disc lemma, Q = oo regularity, and Li asymptotics. Short, but it is a new claim on an open BS conjecture, so it deserves its own referee, especially the claim that poles lie only in {0,1,oo,Disc} and the a0-adic evaluation. It would recover BS Prop 3.1 and Prop ResConifold without degeneration.

Optional: extend the generic-Q and rational-reconstruction tests to genus 4-5, check the two unfinished genus-5 logs in critic/, and consider whether the same programme applies to local P2 on its CY subtorus (not examined here; local P2 has no closed form to compare with).
unknown: Whether LC_CY has a hidden difficulty in a line of s.3-s.9 that I did not read in full. I regard this as unlikely but it is not excluded; the evidence is hand checks of key identities and tests to k <= 10 (L1) and k <= 6 (E_11).
Results of my two genus-5 runs, unfinished at the time of this report. Genus-5 evidence on T_CY therefore remains Report 1's single sample near Q = 1.
No proof that per-decorated-graph polar coefficients are polynomials in (u, a0^2) (Report 2's observation). It is not needed for the extension.
No conceptual reason yet for the flop identity F_g(0) = F_g^flop(0), beyond it being a consequence of the closed form and tested for g <= 6.
Report 2's observation that the colour-2 class is free was not re-tested by me. It is not needed.
Nothing here has been refereed. The classification of steps as established rests on my own hand re-derivation and on the existing proof's refereeing status.
